candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

work_history.title: Clinical Director
work_history.summary: Provide clinical leadership and oversight for behavioral health and substance use treatment services, supporting the delivery of safe, ethical, evidence-based, and recovery-oriented care. Provide clinical oversight and leadership for treatment services, ensuring clinical programming is implemented consistently and aligns with organizational, licensing, and accreditation requirements. Conduct comprehensive clinical assessments and determine appropriate ASAM level of care and treatment placement based on presenting needs, risk factors, withdrawal concerns, mental health symptoms, and recovery environment. Support clinical staff with diagnostic formulation, treatment planning, clinical interventions, documentation, and ongoing evaluation of client progress. Provide individual and group clinical supervision, case consultation, mentoring, and professional development to counselors and other assigned staff. Facilitate interdisciplinary treatment team meetings and clinical case consultations to promote coordinated, clinically appropriate care. Review clinical documentation and provide feedback regarding assessment quality, treatment plans, progress notes, group documentation, and continuity of care. Promote the integration of evidence-based practices, trauma-informed care, motivational interviewing, client-centered interventions, and recovery-oriented approaches throughout clinical programming. Monitor the delivery of daily clinical programming and address barriers affecting treatment quality, staff performance, client engagement, and continuity of care. Assist facility leadership with program development, clinical process improvement, staff training, and implementation of new services. Support compliance with applicable NC DHHS regulations, CARF standards, ASAM Criteria, organizational policies, and clinical documentation requirements. Maintain a safe, structured, therapeutic environment and provide or coordinate crisis intervention and clinical response when indicated. Collaborate with medical, behavioral health, nursing, case management, and facility leadership teams to address complex client needs and promote continuity of care. Advocate for clients and incorporate client-centered perspectives into treatment planning, discharge planning, and recovery goals. Maintain accurate and timely clinical records and ensure completion of required documentation, training, and compliance activities.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with the Adolescent Wellness Academy as you expand into North Carolina. With more than 20 years of experience in adolescent behavioral health, residential and PHP/IOP leadership, clinical operations, and program development, I have built a career dedicated to helping teens and families navigate high stress moments with clarity, compassion, and evidence based support. As a licensed Marriage and Family Therapist, the mission and values of AWA align deeply with my own leadership philosophy and the environments I strive to create.
My entrepreneurial background includes creating, launching and scaling inpatient and outpatient programs, overseeing multidisciplinary clinical and operational teams, and building high quality workflows that support strong outcomes and regulatory compliance. I have led admissions processes, treatment planning, crisis response, and discharge coordination while ensuring documentation quality, accreditation readiness, and risk management. 
I am particularly energized by the opportunity to lead AWA’s first North Carolina facility. I have a proven track record of building values driven cultures where staff feel supported, challenged, and connected to a shared mission. My leadership style is collaborative and people first, clear, and accountable, rooted in radical candor, consistent feedback, and a commitment to helping teams grow. I am skilled at developing talent, managing performance, and fostering environments where clinicians and staff can deliver exceptional care.
I would love the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s expansion, and create a premier resource for adolescents and their families seeking behavioral health services. Thank you for your consideration, and I look forward to the possibility of contributing to AWA’s mission and supporting the successful launch of your North Carolina clinic.
Sincerely,
Dr. Sarah Stuchell, PhD, LMFT

candidates.cover_letter:
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC
Statesville, North Carolina
rorabaughapril@gmail.com
813-842-6018

October 14, 2026


Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor with an Ed.D. in Community Care and Counseling: Traumatology and more than 15 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, and program leadership, I bring a strong commitment to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care to adolescents and families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with youth experiencing complex behavioral health challenges, trauma histories, family instability, and barriers to accessing appropriate treatment. In my leadership role with Partners Health Management, I have overseen behavioral health initiatives across a 15-county service area, supervised multidisciplinary teams, and helped develop and implement specialized programs designed to improve access to services, strengthen care coordination, and reduce unnecessary higher levels of care.  One of my greatest professional strengths is combining clinical expertise with operational leadership. I have experience supporting clinical decision-making, establishing effective workflows, monitoring quality and compliance, mentoring staff, and collaborating with families, community providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies. I understand the importance of developing a clinical environment where staff feel supported, families feel heard, and adolescents receive individualized, evidence-based treatment.

My doctoral research focused on the experiences of social workers placing youth in residential treatment within North Carolina's child welfare system. This work further strengthened my understanding of the challenges adolescents and families face when appropriate community-based behavioral health services are unavailable. I am particularly passionate about developing programs that intervene earlier, promote stability, and help youth receive effective treatment in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

The opportunity to contribute to the development and leadership of Adolescent Wellness Academy's North Carolina program is especially appealing. I would welcome the opportunity to help establish a strong clinical culture, support staff development, build community partnerships, and ensure that adolescents and families receive compassionate, effective, and accountable care.  Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to adolescent mental health could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's success.

Sincerely,
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization. With a career in healthcare spanning more than 25 years, beginning in 1998 as a Unit Secretary and progressing to Clinic Administrator II, I have developed a strong foundation in healthcare operations, team leadership, staff development, and clinic management. Throughout my career, I have remained committed to supporting both the people who deliver care and the patients who depend on it.
My leadership philosophy is rooted in servant leadership. I believe that successful teams are built on trust, collaboration, accountability, and mutual respect. I strive to create an environment where providers, clinical staff, non-clinical team members, and executive leadership work together toward shared goals. I believe that when individuals understand their roles, feel valued for their contributions, and have the support they need to succeed, the entire organization benefits.
My experience includes clinic operations and administration, improving clinic profitability, training and onboarding new team members, and ensuring that staff and providers remain compliant with required education and training. I understand the importance of balancing operational efficiency and financial performance with employee engagement, regulatory compliance, and quality patient care. I enjoy identifying opportunities for improvement, developing team members, and implementing processes that support both organizational success and a positive workplace culture.
One of my greatest goals as a leader is to foster a workplace where people genuinely enjoy coming to work. I want every team member to feel respected, understand the value of their role, and recognize how their contributions help the organization succeed. I believe that investing in people is essential to building strong teams, improving performance, and creating a culture where employees and the organization can thrive together.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring my years of healthcare experience, collaborative leadership style, and passion for developing people and successful operations to your organization. Sincerely,
Dorothy Hedrick

I would aim to make their first interaction with the organization reassuring and informative, while remaining mindful of professional boundaries, program eligibility, and the importance of connecting individuals with appropriate resources.

As a future social work professional, I value empathy, advocacy, ethical practice, and meeting people where they are. I would welcome the opportunity to apply these values in a role that helps adolescents and families access the care they need. I am eager to contribute to a team that recognizes the importance of making behavioral health services more approachable and ensuring families feel supported from their very first interaction.

Sincerely,

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With years of experience as a Physical Therapy Aide, along with front-desk, patient intake, scheduling, phone communication, and administrative experience, I have developed a strong foundation in patient care and a genuine passion for helping others feel supported, understood, and encouraged throughout their healthcare journey.

Throughout my healthcare experience, I have learned how important it is to make every patient feel welcome, respected, and comfortable. I consider myself a compassionate, positive, and motivating person with strong listening and communication skills. I enjoy building connections with people, understanding their concerns, and helping them feel more confident as they navigate their care. I also have experience handling phone calls, coordinating appointments, maintaining patient records, and managing administrative responsibilities. My remote work experience has further strengthened my ability to stay organized, manage responsibilities independently, and follow through consistently.

In addition, I speak four languages, which allows me to connect with people from diverse backgrounds and appreciate the importance of clear, compassionate communication. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience. I believe that a warm voice, a patient listener, and a supportive first interaction can make a meaningful difference for someone seeking help.

My passion for mental health is also personal. Having a close friend who struggled with mental health challenges helped me recognize how important it is for people to feel heard, supported, and treated without judgment. That experience deepened my desire to be part of an environment where individuals and families can find hope, guidance, and access to the care they need. I would be honored to help make that first step toward treatment feel less intimidating and more reassuring.

Although my professional background has primarily been in physical therapy, many of the skills I have developed are directly transferable to admissions coordination, including patient communication, organization, attention to detail, confidentiality, and compassionate support. I am eager to bring these strengths to your team, continue learning, and contribute to a positive admissions experience for adolescents, adults, and their families.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare experience, multilingual abilities, remote work skills, and genuine commitment to helping others could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I look forward to the possibility of joining your team and helping individuals take an important step toward healing and recovery.

Sincerely,
Riddhiben Parmar

candidates.cover_letter:
Good afternoon,
        I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I believe my combination of behavioral health quality assurance, nursing home intake, insurance verification, and remote work experience makes me a strong candidate for this role. I bring both the administrative skills needed to help move the admissions process forward and an understanding of the importance of treating individuals and families with compassion when they are seeking care.

In my current role with Vibrant Emotional Health, I review 988 crisis calls, chats, and texts to evaluate interaction quality, adherence to established protocols, risk assessment, and appropriate crisis response. This experience has strengthened my ability to recognize concerns, pay attention to important details, assess whether established procedures are followed, and understand the importance of appropriate responses in sensitive situations. Working in crisis services has also reinforced that the way people are treated when they reach out for help matters. I would bring that same level of care, attentiveness, and professionalism to conversations with adolescents and families exploring treatment options.

My previous experience in a nursing home setting also provided me with hands-on experience in intake and insurance verification. This background is particularly relevant to a position that requires gathering information, helping prospective clients navigate admissions requirements, and addressing insurance-related steps. I understand that an organized intake process requires accuracy, follow-through, and clear communication. I would use those skills to help families understand what to expect, identify the next steps in the admissions process, and move forward without unnecessary confusion.

I also bring experience working remotely, where independence, accountability, organization, and consistent communication are important. My quality assurance background has further developed my attention to detail and appreciation for accurate documentation and established procedures. I understand that admissions coordination involves more than answering inquiries; it requires keeping track of outstanding steps, following up appropriately, and helping ensure that people do not get lost in the process of seeking services.

As I pursue my Master of Social Work, I continue to strengthen my understanding of behavioral health, person-centered care, and the challenges individuals and families may face when trying to access support. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine my administrative and behavioral health experience with my commitment to helping people connect with appropriate services. I would value the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate the admissions process with clarity, respect, and compassion while supporting the team’s efforts to maintain an organized and responsive admissions pipeline.

Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in intake, insurance verification, remote work, and behavioral health quality assurance could benefit Adolescent Wellness Academy and the families it serves.

Best regards,
Nycole Alexandre

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. With over 10 years of experience in behavioral health and seven years in education, I bring a strong background in supporting individuals and families, understanding behavioral health needs, and connecting people with appropriate services and resources.

I hold a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and a Master’s degree in Human Services, along with certifications as a Certified Anger Management Specialist (CAMS) and in Youth Mental Health First Aid (YMHFA). Throughout my professional career, I have worked with adolescents and adults in behavioral health and educational settings, gaining valuable experience in communication, assessing individual needs, providing support, and maintaining professionalism when navigating sensitive situations.

My experience has strengthened my ability to build rapport, communicate with compassion, maintain confidentiality, and assist individuals and families who may be facing challenging circumstances. I understand that seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming experience, particularly for adolescents and their families. I believe it is important to approach each interaction with patience, empathy, and a commitment to helping individuals feel heard, respected, and informed.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it aligns with both my professional background and my passion for helping young people access the support they need. I am confident that my organizational skills, attention to detail, ability to work independently, and experience in behavioral health would allow me to contribute positively to your admissions team in a virtual environment.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, professional experience, and dedication to supporting adolescents and families align with the goals of your organization.

Sincerely,
LaTressa Moses, M.S., CAMS, YMHFA

I am passionate about helping individuals overcome barriers, build on their strengths, and work toward long-term recovery and personal stability. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my education, experience, and commitment to serving vulnerable populations to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and experience align with the needs of your team.
Terri Stanford

candidates.cover_letter:
Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
October 20, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent calls about a struggling teenager, or an adult finally reaches out about their substance use, the first voice they hear matters. I have spent more than 20 years being that voice, and I would love to bring that experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator.
My career has been built on admissions, assessment, and referral work. At National Healthcare Associates, I handled inbound referrals from several hospital systems at once for multiple facilities, screened each client against admission criteria, and decided whether to accept, deny, or refer them elsewhere. I verified benefits, secured Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial authorizations, and advocated directly with insurers to keep admissions from stalling. Before that, I spent 17 years as Regional Clinical Admissions Director for Kindred Healthcare, managing the full referral to admission cycle for adults with psychiatric and behavioral needs, including co-occurring drug and alcohol use disorders.
I am used to owning my pipeline without daily direction. At Kindred I independently ran a four-state territory, building relationships with case managers, social workers, and discharge planners both virtually and in person, and following up consistently until every referral had a clear outcome. That work generated enough admissions that the organization opened additional units and a new facility. I am comfortable working in CRM and EMR systems, including EPIC, Navi, and Allscripts, and I keep accurate, HIPAA-compliant records.
I also bring a counselor's foundation. I hold an M.S. in Mental Health Counseling and an M.S.Ed. in School Counseling from Syracuse University, my early clinical work included adolescents in day treatment and residential programs, and I served as board president of YouthHarbor. As a Reiki Master Teacher and owner of Beehive Wellness, I meet people in difficult moments with calm and compassion, which is exactly how I would greet your callers.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families and adults move from that first call to a clear next step. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Keli Scott

Dear Hiring Manager,

	I am writing to express my interest in your Virtual Admission Coordinator position through Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a strong background in research and clinical work, I am confident I can contribute effectively to your team through my administrative knowledge, interpersonal skills, compassion, knowledge of substance use and mental health, and data collection experience.

	My bachelor’s degree in psychology from Clemson University has given me the skills to apply statistical analysis and clinical administrative work in my current and past positions. As a Research Assistant at the Medical University of South Carolina, I conduct 20 interviews weekly and record all data through REDCap, Box, and Excel. In these interviews, I lead with empathy and understanding when discussing each patient's circumstances and communicate with their therapist accordingly. While administering assessments during appointments, I ensure that I am clear with the participant about what is expected during our discussions and give them resources when necessary. Each week, I update all logs and REDCap to reflect new data and create weekly meeting agendas to update my team on participant recruitment and enrollment. I have excelled in maintaining IRB materials by submitting all amendments and continuing reviews. My current position highlights skills that I thoroughly enjoy, such as working with participants and conducting assessments, which is why I would be thrilled to apply these to this role.

	My previous role as a Registered Behavior Technician enabled me to focus on child therapy. I implemented Applied Behavior Analysis with patients aged four to sixteen. It was essential to be thoroughly versed in each client's clinical assessments, protocols, and behavioral functioning. Data collection was the main focus of this position, so I excelled at meeting each goal and collecting all necessary data points during each session. My data collection was thorough and exceeded expectations, achieving at least 80 percent each time for my client’s learning objective.

In my previous research at Clemson University, I strengthened my interpersonal skills by recruiting deaf and hearing individuals for my research project, which allowed me to receive feedback and learn more about emotion and cognition. I also practiced several assessments with other students to learn the proper language and resources to provide based on each individual's circumstances. My experience throughout school and in my current or past positions has given me thorough experience communicating with individuals about personal topics and finding them the right resources that are applicable. I believe these experiences align with the requirements of your virtual admissions coordinator position, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute them to your team. Thank you for considering my application, and I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you in greater detail.
Sincerely,
Megan Pfizenmayer

I believe every child deserves to feel supported, understood, and accepted, especially during some of the most challenging years of their lives. Adolescence can already be difficult, and when mental health challenges or substance use become part of that journey, having a compassionate support system can make a tremendous difference. This is one of the reasons I am so passionate about the opportunity to join Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Helping people has always been something that brings me a genuine sense of purpose. During my time as a Case Manager with Prevention Central, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals and families facing various challenges. I conducted assessments, developed individualized case plans, identified barriers, coordinated supportive services, and connected clients with community resources. What I enjoyed most was getting to know the individuals I served, listening to their concerns, understanding their circumstances, and working alongside them to find solutions. I learned that no two individuals are the same, and sometimes making a difference begins with simply taking the time to listen and showing someone that their situation matters.

I understand how important the first point of contact can be when a parent reaches out seeking help for their child. They may be frightened, overwhelmed, frustrated, or simply unsure of what to do next.  I believe the person answering that call has an opportunity to provide more than information. They can offer reassurance, compassion, and a sense of hope. I would never want a parent or teenager to feel like they are just another phone call or admission. I want them to feel heard, respected, and supported while helping them move toward the care they need.

In addition to my case management background, I worked remotely as an Intake Coordinator with All County Health Care, where I assisted clients through the intake process, gathered sensitive information, reviewed documentation, verified eligibility, coordinated services, and maintained confidential records. This experience strengthened my ability to work independently, manage multiple responsibilities, communicate professionally, and remain organized in a fast-paced environment. I understand that admissions require both compassion and urgency because individuals and families seeking treatment should not have to experience unnecessary delays in accessing care.

I am currently nearing completion of my Bachelor of Social Work, a goal that means a great deal to me because I know this is the field where my heart belongs. My training in Trauma-Informed Care, Motivational Interviewing, Mental Health First Aid, and suicide prevention has further strengthened my commitment to meeting people where they are and treating every individual with dignity and understanding. Although my direct admissions experience has not been specifically within a substance use treatment facility, I bring years of transferable experience in intake, case management, client advocacy, and working with vulnerable populations. I am confident in my ability to learn your admissions processes and contribute positively to your team.

What resonates with me most about your mission is the belief that healing happens through connection, compassion, and community.  Families need to know they are not alone in navigating these challenges. While an Admissions Coordinator may not provide the treatment itself, I believe we play an important role in helping families take that first step toward healing.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to interview. I am not simply looking for another job. I am looking for an opportunity to continue making a difference in the lives of individuals and families

Sincerely,
Stacy Scott
 754-273-4930

I understand the importance of building trust, responding to concerns with empathy, maintaining confidentiality, and helping people navigate what can often be an overwhelming process.

I believe my combination of behavioral health admissions experience, strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and compassionate approach would make me a valuable addition to Adolescence Wellness Academy. I am especially interested in the opportunity to apply my experience in a setting focused on supporting adolescents and their families, where clear communication, patience, and a commitment to quality care are essential.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication to behavioral health can contribute to the mission of Adolescence Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Master of Science in Criminal Behavior, a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare administration, family services, and the legal field, I have developed strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills that I believe would translate well into this position. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to support adolescents, adults, and families as they navigate the process of seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

During my time at Bellbrook Family Practice, I gained extensive experience communicating with patients, coordinating appointments, managing medical records, and serving as a point of contact between patients, healthcare providers, and pharmacies. I regularly handled high volumes of phone calls, responded to patient inquiries, coordinated paperwork, and maintained sensitive medical information. This experience taught me the importance of patience, accuracy, confidentiality, and clear communication, particularly when assisting individuals who may be experiencing uncertainty or frustration.

Additionally, my internship with the Greene County Family Visitation Center allowed me to work directly with children and families navigating challenging circumstances. Through supervised visitation services, behavioral observations, and court-related documentation, I developed a greater understanding of the importance of providing compassionate, nonjudgmental support while maintaining professional boundaries. My current position with the Montgomery County Prosecutor’s Office has further strengthened my ability to manage confidential information, maintain detailed records, and balance multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced professional environment.

My graduate education has also provided me with a deeper understanding of psychological disorders, substance use, behavioral health assessment, and the social and environmental factors that influence mental health. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be an overwhelming experience, particularly for adolescents and families who may be unfamiliar with the process. I would welcome the opportunity to help make that first interaction a positive one by providing clear information, reassurance, and consistent follow-through.

I am enthusiastic about the possibility of contributing to an organization dedicated to making behavioral healthcare more accessible. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my educational background, healthcare experience, and commitment to supporting individuals and families could contribute to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Dear Members of the Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at the Adolescent Wellness Academy. In my current role as a High School and Community-Based Care Specialist at Centerstone of Indiana, I work daily on the frontlines of youth mental health. I actively coordinate care plans, conduct client interviews, and deliver crisis interventions for adolescents navigating severe personal and emotional challenges. This role requires a high degree of empathy, rapid clinical problem-solving, and a deep understanding of behavioral health—qualities that are essential when answering an inquiry from a parent or teenager in crisis. Furthermore, my previous tenure at L.A.S.E.R. Project Inc. allowed me to support families heavily impacted by substance abuse and mental health adjustment issues, giving me a comprehensive perspective on the systemic support systems these youth require.
The "virtual" aspect of this coordinator role aligns seamlessly with my entrepreneurial background. I am highly adept at utilizing virtual communication tools, managing digital scheduling systems, and establishing immediate, cross-cultural rapport with clients across varying time zones, including the US, UK, and Australasia. I know how to create a warm, welcoming, and structured environment through a digital screen or phone call, ensuring that anxious families feel heard, validated, and safely guided.
Additionally, I bring a robust administrative toolkit, including specialized knowledge of individualized assessments, state compliance frameworks, and active clinical certifications such as CANS 6+ / ANSA and Psychological First Aid. I understand the vital importance of accurate data collection during the admissions process to ensure seamless transition into active treatment.
I am incredibly drawn to the Adolescent Wellness Academy’s holistic mission to treat adolescent mental health and substance use. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical insight, virtual operational experience, and passion for youth advocacy can serve your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Miggin M. Hutson, M.S.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the **Virtual Admissions Coordinator: Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment** position. With my  experience supporting individuals with behavioral health needs and mental illness, I am confident that my clinical support skills, compassion, communication abilities, and dedication to patient care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my previous role at a 140-bed private psychiatric hospital, I provided care and support to adult patients ranging from geriatric individuals to returning veterans. Working under the direction of nursing and medical staff, I helped patients adjust to new routines, participate in social and therapeutic activities, and complete daily living tasks. I monitored patient behavior, maintained appropriate boundaries, assessed safety concerns, and responded effectively to crisis situations, including assisting with restraints when necessary to prevent injury.

In addition to my direct patient-care experience, I have developed strong skills in behavioral health referrals, admissions, and intake coordination. I am comfortable answering inbound calls and responding to inquiries from clients, parents and guardians, families, referral sources, and healthcare providers. I communicate with patience, empathy, and professionalism while gathering essential information, identifying immediate concerns, and helping families understand available treatment options.

I am familiar with explaining Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP) in clear, caring, and easy-to-understand language. I understand that families seeking adolescent mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing significant stress, and I approach each interaction with sensitivity, respect, and a nonjudgmental attitude. I can help families understand program expectations, levels of care, next steps, and the admissions process while ensuring that urgent safety concerns are communicated promptly to the appropriate clinical staff.

My additional qualifications include:

- Answering inbound calls and responding professionally to inquiries from adolescents, parents, guardians, families, providers, and referral sources  
- Gathering accurate demographic, clinical, insurance, and referral information during initial conversations  
- Screening prospective clients for program fit based on presenting concerns, treatment needs, age, safety considerations, and level of care  
- Explaining PHP, IOP, mental health, and substance use treatment services in a clear and compassionate manner  
- Recognizing potential safety concerns and escalating urgent situations according to established protocols  
- Verifying insurance eligibility and benefits and assisting with authorization-related information  
- Coordinating clinical assessments, intake appointments, admission dates, and required paperwork  
- Communicating with families, providers, clinicians, and other members of the treatment team to support a smooth admissions process  
- Following up consistently with every caller until the individual is scheduled, connected with services, or appropriately referred elsewhere  
- Maintaining accurate and timely documentation in CRM and electronic medical record systems  
- Entering referral and admissions information accurately while protecting confidential patient information  
- Completing documentation in accordance with HIPAA requirements and organizational policies  
- Tracking referrals, follow-up activity, scheduling status, and outcomes to ensure that no inquiry is overlooked  
- Remaining organized, responsive, and professional while managing multiple calls, referrals, and admissions tasks  
- Monitoring patient safety, behavior, vital signs, and overall condition in a psychiatric hospital setting  
- Supporting patients with personal care, daily activities, socialization, and rehabilitation  
- Remaining calm and effective during high-stress conversations and crisis situations  

I am passionate about helping adolescents and families connect with the appropriate behavioral health and substance use treatment services. My combination of hands-on psychiatric experience, referral coordination, insurance verification, admissions support, documentation, and strong interpersonal skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your virtual admissions team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of your organization. I look forward to hearing from you.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over five years of experience in behavioral health and substance use recovery, including client admissions, intake coordination, documentation, and compassionate client support, I bring a strong foundation in helping individuals navigate treatment and access the care they need.

In my current role as a Recovery Specialist at High Point Treatment Center, I complete client admissions and intakes, maintain accurate documentation, support compliance with program requirements, and help facilitate smooth transitions into treatment. Working in a structured behavioral health setting serving individuals with mental health and substance use disorders has strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, recognize client needs, maintain confidentiality, and prioritize safety. Being recognized as Employee of the Year in March 2024 reflects my commitment to professionalism, reliability, and the quality of care I provide.

I understand that the admissions process is often the first meaningful connection a client or family has with a treatment program. I would approach every inquiry with patience, compassion, and clear communication while helping callers understand their options and navigate the next steps toward care. My experience with intake procedures, data entry, documentation, and CRM software has prepared me to manage information accurately, maintain organized workflows, and follow through on important details. I am also comfortable working within established procedures and handling sensitive information with the discretion and confidentiality required in behavioral health.

In addition to my clinical support experience, my previous management roles strengthened my organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills. I managed competing priorities, maintained accurate records, coached team members, and ensured consistent follow-through in fast-paced environments. These experiences have prepared me to manage an admissions pipeline, coordinate multiple responsibilities, and remain accountable in a remote position.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines my behavioral health experience with my passion for helping people take meaningful steps toward recovery. I would welcome the opportunity to support both adolescent mental health services and adult substance use treatment by helping prospective clients and their families feel heard, informed, and supported from their first contact through the admissions process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, admissions and intake skills, and commitment to compassionate client care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,
Alison Vasques

Kris Secor
Barberville, FL

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

Howdy! I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy because this role reflects the kind of work I have spent years doing: showing up for people when they are struggling, building trust when trust does not come easily, and helping individuals feel supported without judgment.
I bring more than seven years of direct behavioral health experience working with children, adolescents, adults, and older adults facing complex mental health, behavioral, and co-occurring substance use challenges. At Promises Behavioral Health, I supported adults ages 18 to 81 in residential and partial hospitalization settings. My work required constant observation, strong boundaries, de-escalation, crisis response, accurate documentation working with Kipu, teamwork with clinicians, and—perhaps most importantly—the ability to connect with people who were overwhelmed, guarded, resistant, or simply having a very difficult day.
Before that, at Halifax Behavioral Health, I worked with at-risk children and adolescents ages 4 to 17. That experience taught me how much can be communicated without words and how important consistency, patience, calmness, and genuine human connection are when someone does not yet feel safe enough to engage.
Those same lessons have followed me throughout nearly three decades of equine work. Through my current business, Healed By The Horse, I create individualized experiences centered on trust, emotional awareness, regulation, confidence, and connection. Horses have reinforced something I already knew from behavioral health: you cannot force trust. You earn it by being present, observant, consistent, and authentic.
That is what draws me to remote work with Adolescent Wellness Academy.
I understand that meaningful mental health is not achieved by treating a diagnosis while overlooking the person living with it. People need to know that someone sees them, hears them, respects their experience, and will continue showing up. I would bring that mindset—along with substantial hands-on behavioral health experience, strong observational skills, compassion, professional boundaries, and a steady presence—to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role.
I am also comfortable working independently, communicating virtually, documenting electronically via Kipu, learning new systems, and collaborating closely with multidisciplinary care teams. The opportunity to provide meaningful support within a virtual treatment environment is especially appealing to me.
I would be proud to bring my experience, patience, intuition, and very genuine commitment to helping people to Adolescent Wellness Academy. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how I could contribute to your team and, most importantly, to the individuals you serve.

Warmly,

Kris Secor

candidates.cover_letter:
Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in psychology, behavioral health, crisis support, and working directly with children and families, I was immediately drawn to this opportunity because of the importance you place on making the first point of contact compassionate, supportive, and clear.

Throughout my experience in behavioral health, I have learned that the way someone is treated during their first interaction can significantly affect whether they feel comfortable accepting help. In my work as a Behavioral Therapist/RBT, I have provided individualized behavioral support to children, communicated closely with parents and caregivers, maintained confidential documentation, assisted with scheduling and insurance coordination, and supported families through challenging behavioral situations. This experience has required patience, organization, professionalism, and the ability to communicate complicated information in a way that families can easily understand.

My crisis-support experience has strengthened these skills even further. As a Youth Crisis Counselor and Suicide Prevention Crisis Line Volunteer, I supported individuals during highly emotional and vulnerable moments through active listening, crisis intervention, risk and safety assessment, de-escalation, and connection to appropriate resources. These experiences taught me how to remain calm when someone on the other end of the conversation may be scared, overwhelmed, frustrated, or unsure of what to do next.

I also understand that effective admissions coordination requires more than compassion. It requires strong follow-through. My professional experience includes scheduling, insurance coordination, detailed documentation, maintaining confidentiality, communicating with families, and independently managing responsibilities. I am comfortable working with technology and learning new systems, and I understand the importance of accurate, timely, and HIPAA-compliant documentation when working in behavioral health.

I am especially interested in this position because it combines the administrative side of behavioral healthcare with direct human connection. I would value the opportunity to help a parent searching for treatment for their teenager, an individual seeking help for substance use or mental health concerns, or a provider trying to connect someone with an appropriate level of care. Even when a program is not the right fit, I believe every person deserves to leave that interaction feeling heard, respected, and clearer about what they can do next.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my behavioral health experience, crisis-support background, communication skills, and commitment to compassionate care to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Brianna Otero
